nodes.label: NDD Format (Naturalized DICOM Data)
nodes.rationale: Experimental JSON representation of DICOM datasets with human-readable keyword names instead of tag numbers; the display examples dump datasets in this format so developers can inspect the inner structure of DICOM data directly in the browser.

nodes.label: Legacy dcmjs.DICOMWEB client API
nodes.rationale: The IHE Invoke Image Display example instantiates new dcmjs.DICOMWEB({...}) with studies/series/instances/instance QIDO+WADO methods; no dicomweb module exists in the current src/ tree, so this is a legacy API surface the example depends on.

nodes.label: Legacy dcmjs.data.DICOMZero API
nodes.rationale: The TCIA example constructs new dcmjs.data.DICOMZero() from the bundled library instead of loading /helpers/DICOMZero.js; current src/ has no DICOMZero module, so this example targets an older dcmjs build.

nodes.label: Packed Dictionary System
nodes.rationale: Shipping the full DICOM dictionary as JS object literals cost megabytes parsed at every import. Base64-encoded typed-array tables decoded once on first use dropped import cost from 181 ms to 19 ms (9.5x), keeping hot-path lookups at binary-search-plus-memo cost while making startup nearly free.

nodes.label: Lazy nameMap Getter
nodes.rationale: In 0.x the ~5000-entry keyword-to-entry nameMap was built at import time; 1.0 builds it in a memoizing static getter on first access so import cost no longer pays for it.

nodes.label: Event-Stream Four-Layer Model
nodes.rationale: Separates source representations, the event-stream contract, listeners/writers, and the retained naturalized representation so readers, writers, naturalizers, validators, and anonymizers all compose on one contract.

nodes.label: Event-Stream Contract (Hybrid Push Core)
nodes.rationale: The contract is a synchronous push core with an async-iterator adapter layered on top: the push core keeps the hot path allocation-free, the adapter offers for-await ergonomics. Backpressure is applied out of band (setDrain/awaitDrain) only at defined checkpoints.

nodes.label: Loss Preservation Invariant
nodes.rationale: A generator emits every observed value and item regardless of declared VM; cardinality enforcement and diagnostics are listener policies, never the stream's, keeping the stream purely loss-preserving.

nodes.label: Source-Agnostic Equivalence
nodes.rationale: Because all sources emit the same contract, the naturalized object is identical across origins; verified across the fixture corpus by naturalizing each fixture from raw bytes, a parsed dict, and DICOMweb JSON.

nodes.label: Getter-Backed Lazy Entries
nodes.rationale: Entries keep the eager { vr, Value, _rawValue } observable shape but Value/_rawValue are accessor properties: the getter materializes and caches on first access; the setter flips the _dirty flag — the seam the passthrough writer is built on. No behavioral cliff, only deferred work.

nodes.label: Windowed Stream Materialization
nodes.rationale: The VR classes were not rewritten: ReadBufferStream {start, stop} windows let materialization run exactly the vr.read call the eager reader made — one small stream allocation per first access is the cost of this correctness-first bridge.

nodes.label: Per-Item Charset Contexts
nodes.rationale: There is no scan in the lazy model, so the decoder is resolved once per dataset at wrap time; sequence items carrying their own 0008,0005 get per-item contexts — exceeding the 0.x reader's single-charset-per-file support.

nodes.label: Whole-File Eager Fallback
nodes.rationale: When the tokenizer rejects a stream outright (truncated files, overrunning lengths, missing part-10 plumbing), the entire read is delegated to the eager core so its exact behavior — including errors and ignoreErrors recovery points — is reproduced by running it.

nodes.label: Eager Core Escape Hatch (DCMJS_CORE)
nodes.rationale: The historical eager read loop is kept behind core:'eager'/DCMJS_CORE=eager as a beta-soak escape hatch, not a supported long-term mode; slated for deletion in 1.x once the async reader is re-platformed onto the tokenizer.

nodes.label: Documented Divergences from 0.x Eager Reader
nodes.rationale: Three intentional, test-pinned divergences: value-level errors throw at first access instead of during readFile; ignoreErrors:true returns the full dict with the failing entry undefined instead of truncating (strictly more informative); charset scope applies per dataset/item, diverging only on non-conformant element ordering.

nodes.label: dcmjs Layered Architecture
nodes.rationale: Layer 0 offset tokenizer (dependency-free), layer 1 data model, layer 2 features, edge adapters; arrows only point downward — the parser never imports dcmjs, never touches the dictionary, never decodes character sets, by design.

nodes.label: Derivability Argument (Offsets over Values)
nodes.rationale: Offsets can always produce values (decode lazily, with any charset, or never), but eager values cannot recover offsets — once decoded, the exact framing is gone. Recording offsets is the more fundamental representation, buying lazy reads and byte-faithful writes; startOffset/endOffset were added because dataOffset alone is ambiguous.

nodes.label: @dcmjs/parser Offset Tokenizer Package
nodes.rationale: The dicom-parser codebase vendored whole as a private, dependency-free workspace package, then deliberately diverged. No tag dictionary and no charset handling — those are data-layer concerns injected via vrCallback.

nodes.label: Offset Element Model (tagValue/startOffset/endOffset)
nodes.rationale: Every element is one object literal with all fields present (one hidden class, a deliberate perf property). tagValue, startOffset, endOffset are dcmjs additions: the complete on-disk span is not recoverable after the fact and is the prerequisite for the passthrough writer.

nodes.label: Intentional Divergences from Upstream dicom-parser
nodes.rationale: Safe because the vendored parser has no external consumers: UV/SV/OV framing, eager-aligned unknown-VR fallback, explicit FFFE delimiter framing, deflate stream start fix, warnings.push crash fix, omitPrivateAttributes rename — each pinned by the 245-test parser suite.

nodes.label: AsyncDicomReader Streaming Reader
nodes.rationale: Reads DICOM from chunked input with bounded memory (ensureAvailable/consume). Still runs its own header/element logic rather than the tokenizer — deliberate, because the tokenizer assumes one contiguous buffer and the re-platform was judged the hardest piece of the 1.0 rewiring.

nodes.label: 1.x Streaming Re-platform Plan
nodes.rationale: Run the parser's element readers over contiguous windows SplitDataView can guarantee, point the meta-group read at the parser's Part 10 header reader, confine SplitDataView to the streaming layer — after which the legacy eager read loop can be deleted.

nodes.label: Backpatching Re-encoder
nodes.rationale: Replaces the 0.x per-element temp stream and double copy: write directly into the destination, reserve the length field, backpatch it with writeUint16At/writeUint32At after the VR class encodes.

nodes.label: Passthrough Fast Path
nodes.rationale: A never-edited lazy entry knows its exact on-disk encoding (_sourceSpan), so the writer skips encoding entirely and copies whole SQ subtrees and encapsulated PixelData runs in one subarray each — byte-identical, header to delimiter.

nodes.label: Big 16 UN Substitution
nodes.rationale: An 8-byte short explicit header cannot be backpatched into the 12-byte Big 16 layout, so the writer decides up front: fixed-size VRs emit the right header immediately; variable-length values are screened by a deliberately over-estimating valueByteUpperBound and only possible overflows take the measured path.

nodes.label: Zero-Copy Windows (writeRawBytes)
nodes.rationale: Spans of 64 KB or more become read-only zero-copy windows over the source buffer instead of copies; window chunks are marked read-only so a misdirected length backpatch can never corrupt the caller's source buffer.

nodes.label: Assignment-Based Dirty Tracking
nodes.rationale: Dirtiness is assignment-based by design: setters flip _dirty and bump _nestedDirtCount up the enclosing-sequence chain; structural sequence edits are re-verified at write time (sqStructureDiverged). In-place mutation is undetectable by design and documented.

nodes.label: Byte-Identity Guarantee
nodes.rationale: For an eligible file read by the lazy core and written back with zero edits, same syntax, default options, and a passthrough-safe charset, the dataset body is reproduced byte-for-byte — a guarantee 0.x never had, pinned by round-trip suites over an adversarial corpus.

nodes.label: Deflate on Write
nodes.rationale: Per PS3.10 A.5 the preamble, DICM, and meta group are written uncompressed and the body raw-deflated (RFC 1951); a deflated source's spans index the inflated body buffer, so passthrough composes and only the deflate wrapper is recomputed.

nodes.label: Gate Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Two mechanically enforced rules: never regress the tokenizer (bench:parser geomean <= 1.10 vs published dicom-parser, bundle gate proves the parser stays a dependency-free island), and both cores stay equivalent (full 635-test suite green on lazy and DCMJS_CORE=eager) until the eager core is deleted.

nodes.label: 1.0 Rewiring Roadmap (R0-R8)
nodes.rationale: The engineering plan and log for merging dicom-parser into dcmjs: one lazy read core, one passthrough write path, a typeable tree-shakable surface, honest semantics. Absorbed the former docs/REWIRING-PLAN.md.

nodes.label: Founding Decisions
nodes.rationale: dcmjs becomes a pnpm monorepo with the tokenizer vendored whole; 1.0 is a breaking release with no dicom-parser shim and no 0.x compat layer; the eager reader is to be deleted once equivalence passes (kept as escape hatch in execution); internal tag identity is numeric everywhere.

nodes.label: Open 1.0 API Decisions
nodes.rationale: Four open decisions needing owner sign-off: VM-driven scalar collapse, keep/drop ISO_IR 192 normalize-on-read, binary values as zero-copy views by default, and the public dict key format.

nodes.label: Normalize-on-Read to ISO_IR 192
nodes.rationale: dcmjs deliberately decodes with the declared charset, rewrites the stored SpecificCharacterSet Value to ISO_IR 192 (preserving the original in _rawValue), and encodes UTF-8 on write so the output stays consistent. Whether to keep this quirk is an open 1.0 API decision.

nodes.label: charsetPassthroughSafe Gate
nodes.rationale: Passthrough requires UTF-8 re-encoding to be byte-stable against the source, so the gate is deliberately conservative: only absent/empty/ASCII/UTF-8 top-level charsets qualify; ISO_IR 100 sources always re-encode today, with a per-element ASCII fast path planned for 1.x.

nodes.label: Deflated Transfer Syntax Handling
nodes.rationale: Deflate is a stream-level wrapper so inflation is eager (no per-element inflate is possible); conversion to/from deflated is just a meta edit because the body encoding is ELE on both sides.

nodes.label: 0.x Uncompressed-Deflate Bug Fix
nodes.rationale: 0.x wrote an uncompressed body under a deflated TSUID, silently producing files conforming readers reject; 1.0 makes the declared syntax and the bytes agree, so 0.x workarounds (rewriting the TSUID) can be dropped.

nodes.label: DicomEventStream API
nodes.rationale: Wraps a re-runnable source so one stream can drive several sinks; .from() auto-detects bytes vs dataset vs DICOM JSON.

nodes.label: Event-Stream Sinks (toNaturalized/toDicomWebJson/toPart10/toDataSet)
nodes.rationale: toPart10 is a thin layer over the canonical DicomDict.write; byte-identical Part 10 round-tripping is an explicit non-goal of the event pipeline — that is served by the lazy read + passthrough writer.

nodes.label: Naturalized Model (VM-Driven Cardinality)
nodes.rationale: Value shapes follow the attribute's declared VM, not how many values happen to be present — fixing the instance-driven scalar/array instability. Single-item sequences read straight through; PN values keep DICOMweb component shape; over-precision numerics retain source strings.

nodes.label: Instance-Driven Single-Value Collapse
nodes.rationale: The same attribute can be a scalar in one file and an array in another because collapse is instance-driven, not VM-driven — the single most common dcmjs 0.x complaint and the subject of an open 1.0 decision.

nodes.label: Private-Tag Loss on Denaturalize
nodes.rationale: denaturalizeDataset only emits names found in the name map; hex-named entries are dropped with only a warning, so a naturalize/denaturalize round trip silently loses private data. Edit the tag-keyed dict directly to preserve them.

nodes.label: Error-Timing Semantics
nodes.rationale: The lazy core changes when errors surface, not whether: structural errors throw at readFile time, value-level errors at first access — a direct consequence of laziness (work that does not happen at read time cannot fail at read time).

nodes.label: ignoreErrors Full-Dict Recovery
nodes.rationale: Instead of truncating the dict at a failing element like 0.x, the lazy core returns the full dict and resolves only the failing entry to undefined with one warning — strictly more informative.

nodes.label: Assignment-Based Editing Rules
nodes.rationale: Only assignments (entry.Value = ..., entry._rawValue = ..., upsertTag) are tracked; in-place mutation of a materialized value leaves the entry looking clean and the passthrough writer silently emits the original bytes.

nodes.label: Structural Sequence Edit Detection
nodes.rationale: Item dicts are plain objects so key adds/deletes and item pushes/splices bypass every setter; because such edits would otherwise be silently dropped, the writer re-verifies every materialized sequence's structure against the parsed source at write time.

nodes.label: The 1.0 Merge Story
nodes.rationale: dcmjs 1.0 merges two long-lived projects into one engine: the dicom-parser tokenizer became the read core, reading is lazy by default, the writer is byte-faithful, and everything lives in one pnpm monorepo — same public API shape on a new engine.

nodes.label: Migrating from dicom-parser
nodes.rationale: The dicom-parser repository is dormant; its tokenizer lives on inside dcmjs. No compatibility shim will be published under the dicom-parser npm name — dcmjs 1.0 is the migration target; the raw tier stays private until the subpath export split.

nodes.label: Measured Performance Numbers
nodes.rationale: Vendored tokenizer geomean ~0.84-0.85 vs published dicom-parser (faster on every corpus file); writer 1.76x on SR trees and 3.23x on large values; 199 MB to 4 KB allocation drop; dictionary import 181 ms to 19 ms. All measured on one developer machine — relative indicators, not absolute promises.

nodes.label: Standing Performance Gates
nodes.rationale: bench:parser (geomean <= 1.10, single file <= 1.25), gate:parser-bundle (self-containment, <= 120 kB, no pako, side-effect-free import), the byte-identity suite, and dual-core equivalence (635 + 245 tests) must all stay green.

nodes.label: Laziness Characteristics
nodes.rationale: Parse cost is independent of value sizes; memory is ~1x the file because the source buffer is retained and binary values are views; laziness wins when touching a subset — a workload touching every value approaches eager cost plus getter indirection.
